metadata.title: This Week's Fixes.
metadata.note: Weekly update (changelog framing, per creator). Narrator Muskan, @HumanitariansAI, banner 'Vendor Intelligence'. Three tasks: (1) wrong-company news stored as real signals, (2) deprecated lib + version locks, (3) broken collectors / better wrong-company check / observability. Bookends render (composer/verdict/handoff/outro via Claude Remotion comps); body B01-B06 are house-style 4K PIL cards generated by make_cards.py. DOUBLE-CHECK LAW — exact figures from the creator's change log: 72 of 76 Scale AI signals were other companies'; 21 counted as funding; score 75 with 25 pts from an Indian ed-tech raise; 'raised $1B to scale AI' (scale = verb); cleaned 72 rows, backup first; retired model swapped, ~half cost, token limit raised; deprecated lib builds all 5 agents; 4 dependencies version-locked, 2 breakages this week; role-lookup check 10/16 → 16/16, works for unconfigured names; ~1 in 4 checks failed and old code failed OPEN (assumed match) → now rejects; observability stored a summary not the real request/response, and logged phantom calls that never happened.

beats.narration_text: Hey, I'm Muskan. This week was mostly cleanup on the vendor-intelligence system, and it got uncomfortable. A health score built on the wrong company's news, monitoring that logged fake data, and a check that would fail silently. Here's what broke, and what I fixed.

props.command: What broke in the vendor-intel system this week — and what did I actually fix?
output: 1 · a score built on the wrong company

beats.narration_text: Start with the worst one. The system finds news by searching each company's name. That breaks when the name is also a normal phrase. Scale AI is the nightmare case: headlines constantly say things like, raised a billion to scale AI, where scale is just a verb. Seventy-two of Scale AI's seventy-six stored signals were actually other companies' news.

show.event: the four damning stats snap in

card.title: Wrong-Company News.
card.subtitle: when a name is also a phrase

items.quote: “raised $1B to scale AI” — scale = a verb
25 pts from an Indian ed-tech raise

card.caption: the system searched by name — but the name was a common English phrase
card.footer: FOUND BY NAME · BUT THE NAME WASN'T THE STORY

beats.narration_text: That fed the financial health score. Scale AI showed a seventy-five, and twenty-five of those points came from an Indian education company's raise. The fix: check how the name is used, not just whether it appears, and only for names that are also ordinary words. I cleaned seventy-two bad rows, backup first, and the score went from a made-up seventy-five to an honest unknown, flagged for review.

show.at: check how the name is used

show.event: the right panel resolves to UNKNOWN (accent)

card.title: Use, Not Just Mention.
card.subtitle: the fix + the cleanup
card.caption: check how the name is USED, not just whether it appears — only for names that are also words

beats.narration_text: Back to the wrong-company check, I made it much stronger. Now the AI has to state what role the company name plays in the headline before it decides. That turns a judgement call into a lookup. Accuracy on unseen cases went from ten out of sixteen to sixteen out of sixteen, and it finally works for companies nobody configured by hand.

show.event: old rule-based vs new role-first panels

card.title: The Check, Hardened.
card.subtitle: judgement → lookup
card.caption: the AI must say what role the company name plays in the headline before it decides
card.footer: 10/16 → 16/16 · NOW WORKS FOR NAMES NOBODY CONFIGURED

beats.narration_text: But testing caught something scary. At the old token limit, about one in four of these checks would fail. And on failure, the old code assumed the article was about the company. So shipping the better check would have silently switched it off for a quarter of all headlines, while the logs looked perfectly fine. I flipped the failure to reject, not accept, matching what the instructions already say: when unsure, say no.

show.event: the right panel resolves to REJECT (accent)

card.title: Fail Closed.
card.subtitle: the bug that would've hidden
card.caption: ~25% of checks failed at the old token limit — and failure used to mean 'accept'

beats.narration_text: The theme of the week: a confident number can be pure noise. Clean the bad inputs, make the system fail closed when it's unsure, and log what actually happened, not a story about it.

artifactLines: Wrong-company news: 72 of 76 Scale AI signals were other companies' — cleaned; 75 → honest UNKNOWN.
The check now asks the name's role before deciding: 10/16 → 16/16, and works for unconfigured names.
Fail closed: an uncertain check now rejects instead of assuming a match (it was failing open ~1 in 4).
Kept it honest + running: real logs (prompt/response/tokens), current model (~half cost), locked deps.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Look at one number your own tools report as a fact, a score, a count, a confidence. Ask where it comes from, and what happens to it when the data behind it is missing. If the answer is, it makes something up, that's your next fix.

props.command: Take one number my tools report as a fact — a score, a count, a confidence. Where does it come from, and what happens to it when the data behind it is missing?
output: if the answer is “it makes one up”
fail closed · log the real thing

beats.narration_text: This week's fixes. More next week. Humanitarians AI.
